home.headline: A standalone inventory program for every shop PC.
home.support: Download it, start it, and work offline. This PC keeps its own database — on Windows, macOS, or Linux. Cloud is only for sharing data with other PCs, not for day-to-day work.
home.whatBody: StockPilot is a bilingual (English / Arabic) retail inventory system. It covers products and catalog, warehouses and stock movements, sales orders and purchase orders, people and payments, registers, and admin tools. Each shop PC runs as its own program. Cloud upload/import is optional when you need to share data between PCs.
home.whoBody: Shop-floor operators run inventory and checkout on this PC with no internet required. Admins configure members and features. A second PC (or a second folder on the same machine) is a full standalone install — own folder, database, and ports — that does not mix with another copy. Linking to hosted cloud is optional when you want to upload or import shared data.
home.setupTitle: Run StockPilot as a standalone program
home.setupIntro: Download → Start StockPilot → sign in → work. No cloud files and no other PC are required. Each folder is isolated (own database and ports) so two installs on one machine do not mix. Sharing via cloud is Part B, only when you need it.
home.osHint: Choose your operating system. The matching tab is selected when this page can detect it.
home.setupStep1BodyWindows: Install Docker Desktop and Node.js LTS (≥ 20). Start Docker Desktop and wait until it is running, then verify in a new Command Prompt or PowerShell:
home.setupStep1BodyMac: Install Docker Desktop and Node.js LTS (≥ 20). Start Docker Desktop and wait until it is running, then verify in a new Terminal:
home.setupStep1BodyLinux: Install Docker Engine and the Compose plugin (or Docker Desktop) and Node.js LTS (≥ 20). Add your user to the docker group if needed, then verify in a new terminal:
home.setupStep2Body: Use Download Now above (develop zip) or git clone. Unzip into its own folder (the directory with docker-compose.yml). Keep each download in its own folder if you run more than one. Do not copy .env from another PC.
home.setupStep3Body: Use the Start file for your OS (or the npm command). It creates this folder’s environment, starts the local database, seeds admin, builds the app, and opens it. Cloud is not used.
home.setupStep3LinuxHint: If the file is not executable yet, run this once in the project folder, then start:
home.setupStep3Options: Daily use: Start StockPilot. Updates: Update StockPilot (same folder; keeps your data).
home.setupStep3NpmHint: Or from a terminal in this folder:
home.setupStep3FreshHint: If something is broken (wipe this folder’s local DB + clean + full setup):
home.setupStep4Title: 4. Open the app and sign in
home.setupStep4Body: Start StockPilot already serves the UI. Open the URL it prints (often http://localhost:8080). Sign in as username admin / password devpass123 — that admin unlocks Control, Admin, Notifications, and Data sync (members do not see those links). Unplug the internet: the app keeps working.
home.setupStep4ServeHint: If you ran only npm run second-pc:setup, serve with STOCKPILOT_UI_PORT from .env (often 8080). Stop only this stack with docker compose down from this folder.
home.cloudHeading: Part B — Share with other PCs (optional)
home.cloudIntro: Skip this for normal work. Use cloud only to upload or import data so another standalone PC can share the same catalog, stock, and orders. This PC stays the local master.
home.cloudStep1Body: Copy .env.cloud.example → .env.cloud.local and set the hosted project URL and anon key.
home.cloudStep2Body: Bake sync keys into the app, then serve again:
home.cloudStep3Body: Copy .env.mirror-auth.example → .env.mirror-auth.local (local URL is http://127.0.0.1: plus this folder’s KONG_HTTP_PORT). Dry-run, then wipe and recreate local Auth:
home.cloudStep3Warning: Mirroring deletes all local Auth users, then recreates them from hosted. Hosted passwords are not copied — everyone gets MIRROR_LOCAL_PASSWORD (default devpass123).
home.cloudStep4Body: Sign in with a mirrored operator, open Admin → Data sync, connect to hosted cloud, and run sync once (upload from this PC or import onto another).
home.setupAfterBody: Each day, run Start StockPilot in the same folder. To get a newer version, run Update StockPilot (keeps volumes and .env). If the stack is broken: npm run second-pc:fresh. Do not copy .env between folders. Re-run Part B only when you use cloud sharing and hosted operators change.

adminSync.title: Data sync
adminSync.subtitle: Cloud is the master: push local rows to hosted Supabase (sales order and PO numbers are kept when that number is not already used on cloud), repair any remaining duplicate document numbers on the cloud, refresh product quantity totals, then pull the full cloud snapshot back to this device.
adminSync.needLocalApp: Data sync is available when the app uses local Supabase (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:54321). Run npm run dev with local URLs, not npm run dev:cloud only.
adminSync.profilesNote: When Auth is missing on the sync **target** (pull from host → local, or push from local → host), the app calls Edge Function `ensure-local-operator-auth` on that project (deploy it on local and hosted; admin-only). Mirrored users sign in with `username`@members.stockpilot.local and the temp password from `OPERATOR_MIRROR_TEMP_PASSWORD` on that function (default devpass123 locally; set the secret on hosted if needed). Passwords are not copied between environments.
adminSync.profilesSkippedToastTitle: {{count}} hosted operator profiles not copied locally
adminSync.profilesSkippedToastDesc: Local Supabase Auth has no row with those user ids, so profile rows cannot be created here. The rest of this sync succeeded. Operators who should sign in on local need matching Auth users (same ids as on the host—often via a dev seed or SQL on local only).
adminSync.rlsNote: Uses your normal Supabase sessions only (no service role in the browser). The hosted user must be allowed by RLS to read and upsert the listed tables.
adminSync.envOk: VITE_SYNC_CLOUD_URL and VITE_SYNC_CLOUD_ANON_KEY are set (e.g. in .env.development).
adminSync.envMissing: Hosted project URL and anon key are not available for Data sync. Add VITE_SYNC_CLOUD_URL and VITE_SYNC_CLOUD_ANON_KEY to .env.development (or .env.development.local), or put your hosted VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY in .env.cloud.local (used for dev and for npm run build), then restart the dev server or rebuild. See .env.example and docs/SECOND_PC.md.
adminSync.cloudCredentialsHint: Use the full email listed under Authentication → Users on your hosted project (e.g. admin@members.stockpilot.local if you created that user there). This is not the same as typing only the short username from the main login screen.
adminSync.connectFailed: Could not sign in to the hosted project.
adminSync.invalidHostedCredentials: Hosted project rejected email or password. Confirm VITE_SYNC_CLOUD_* points at that project, then use the exact Auth user email and password from the hosted dashboard (not your local-only password unless they match).
adminSync.missingEnv: Missing cloud URL or anon key in env.
adminSync.connectFirst: Connect to the hosted project first.
adminSync.resetLocalConfirm: This permanently deletes all mirrored inventory data on this machine (orders, stock, catalog sync tables, alerts, sync queue) and replaces it with a full download from the hosted project. Operator profile rows are not deleted (they are updated from cloud when the same Auth user exists locally). Continue?
adminSync.doneResetLocalToast: Local database was cleared and refreshed from cloud. Pulled {{pulled}} rows. Cloud order repairs before pull: sales {{ordersFixed}}, PO {{poFixed}}.
adminSync.localSupabaseBad: Local Supabase URL missing or not local
adminSync.readinessBlocked: Fix readiness issues (network, env, local URL, cloud sign-in) before syncing.
adminSync.historySubtitle: Recent runs recorded on this database (local Supabase when using npm run dev).
adminSync.cloudPartialWarning: The hosted database may have received only part of this sync, or stock reconciliation on the host failed. Re-run sync after fixing the error, or restore the cloud project from a backup if data looks wrong.
adminSync.syncRecoveredWarning: The first local download step failed, but the app re-pulled the full cloud snapshot and reconciled local stock. Details: {{detail}}
adminSync.doneCloudToast: Cloud master sync finished. Pushed {{pushed}} rows, pulled {{pulled}}. Duplicate sales order numbers repaired on cloud: {{ordersFixed}}. Duplicate PO numbers repaired: {{poFixed}}.
adminSync.progressCounts: Written to cloud: {{pushed}} · Written to local: {{pulled}}
adminSync.doneToast: Sync finished. To cloud: {{pushed}}, to local: {{pulled}}, conflicts resolved: {{conflicts}}, skipped: {{skipped}}.

control.title: Control
control.intro: Turn features on or off for this browser. Each toggle describes what it shows or hides in the app. Non-admin operators also receive server-side permission overrides from Admin → Members; when both disagree, the stricter rule wins for that user.
control.guideCardBody: Use the platform guide for a feature map, the migration guide for recommended import order (warehouses, catalog, CSV, register), Members to create operators and warehouse access, and Data sync when you mirror data between local and hosted Supabase.
control.guideCardFootnote: Some links are hidden when their sidebar or Admin toggles are off—enable them here first if you need those screens.
control.securityNote: These toggles only hide or show UI. They do not block API access. Use database policies for real enforcement.

importPaste.title: Import customers & sellers
importPaste.welcomeBody: Bring customers and sellers from your old sheet. You can add names and old IDs now; phones and balances later. One sheet is enough — map a role column if you have it, otherwise everyone is both customer and supplier.
importPaste.welcomeTip: Paste from Excel. Cloud is not required. You can import the same people again later to fill missing fields.
importPaste.whatToCopyBody:
In Excel, select the header row plus data rows, then Copy.
Include a header row when you can (Name, ID, Phone…).
You do not need every column this time — name is enough to create. Old ID is strongly recommended so a later paste can add phones or balances.
importPaste.pasteHint: Paste the range you copied from Excel.
importPaste.pasteTip: Copy a rectangle in Excel (Ctrl+C / Cmd+C), then paste here. Tabs between columns work best.
importPaste.clipboardDenied: Could not read the clipboard. Paste into the box with Ctrl+V / Cmd+V.
importPaste.emptyPaste: No rows found. Copy a range that includes at least one data row.
importPaste.unmappedOk: Unmapped columns are OK. Only Name is required this pass. Old ID is recommended.
importPaste.nameRequiredMap: Map a column to Name before continuing.
importPaste.needNamedRow: At least one row needs a name (2+ characters).
importPaste.previewHint: {{count}} row(s) will be reviewed. Blank cells will not wipe data already saved.
importPaste.previewTip: Discard rows you do not want. You can edit names before matching.
importPaste.conflictsHint: Rows that match someone already in StockPilot need an action. New rows default to Create.
importPaste.overwriteFilled: Overwrite fields that already have a value
importPaste.separateBlocked: To keep them separate, change the colliding old ID or phone first.
importPaste.applyBody: Create {{created}}, update {{updated}}, skip {{skipped}}. New people start at balance 0. Opening amounts on matched rows apply only if you chose Update or Merge.
importPaste.balancesHint: Set opening balances for people just created, or skip and paste balances later using the same old IDs.
importPaste.balancesTip: Positive = they owe you (customer). For a seller-only row, a positive number means you owe them.
importPaste.noNewForBalances: No new people were created in this pass.
importPaste.doneBody: You can sell. Come back to add phones or balances with the same old IDs.
importPaste.mergeBody: One person will keep both roles. Confirm the signed balance (positive = they owe you, negative = you owe them).
importPaste.sellerMeansPayable: Treat a positive seller amount as money you owe them
importPaste.emptyCta: Start by importing customers and sellers from your old sheet.

adminHub.title: Admin hub & operators
items: Admin hub routes: /admin (cards), Dashboard, Documentation (/admin/documentation), Migration guide (/admin/migration), Members (/admin/members/*), Data sync (/sync when enabled), Reports, Stock movements

stockAlerts.title: Alerts bell
items: Unread stock and system alerts (low stock, sync issues, register/wallet signals, informational notices)
Some alerts are admin-only (for example document replacement after edit-as-replacement); only admins see them in the bell and realtime toast

security.title: Sign-in, members & security
items: Every operator is a Supabase Auth user; the app loads a profiles row (is_admin, feature_overrides, allowed_warehouse_ids) after sign-in.
Only admins may open /admin and /control; route checks use profiles.is_admin, not Control toggles alone.
Control toggles and localStorage shape default UI for this browser; non-admin permissions merge feature_overrides from the server — if either side disables a capability, the operator cannot use it.
Sign-in uses a synthetic email: username@members.stockpilot.local — create the Auth user with that email pattern (the create-member Edge Function does this for you).
Never put the service role key or plaintext operator passwords in VITE_* env or bundled client code; member creation uses the create-member Edge Function with the service role on the server.
Bootstrap the fixed admin in Supabase Dashboard (Auth → Users) or a one-off script: set user_metadata username and is_admin true; password only in Auth.
Apply all SQL migrations before go-live so RLS, registers, multi-warehouse stock, and CSV paths match the app version you deploy.
Logout clears the session from this browser; see Supabase Auth docs for refresh tokens and RLS.

migrationGuide.title: Migration & setup guide
migrationGuide.subtitle: End-to-end path to adopt StockPilot: Auth, members, warehouses, catalog, transfers, optional hosted/local sync, CSV loads, register, and go-live checks.
migrationGuide.intro: Start here: import customers and sellers (paste from Excel). Then locations, catalog, and optional document CSV. Create operators under Admin → Members. Progress saves in this browser only. The Platform guide (/admin/documentation) explains each area in more detail.
migrationGuide.savedLocallyHint: Progress is stored only on this device (localStorage). It is not synced to your account or other browsers.
migrationGuide.resetConfirmDescription: This clears all checkmarks in this browser. It does not delete any data in StockPilot.
migrationGuide.markAllConfirmDescription: Use this if you have already finished migration and only want the checklist to show 100% complete.

people_wizard.title: Import customers and sellers (guided)
people_wizard.body: Open People and run Import customers & sellers. Paste from Excel in passes: names and old IDs first, then balances, then phones. The wizard maps columns, warns when someone is already on the system, and lets you skip, update, merge (net balance), or separate. Phone is optional on the first pass.

plan_exports.title: Export and clean data from the old system
plan_exports.body: Pull customer/supplier lists with consistent phone numbers (used for matching), product codes/SKUs, units, and any opening stock figures. Normalize dates and currencies to match how you will import. Decide what is truly “historical only” vs what you will operate going forward.

env_schema.title: Database and app environment ready
env_schema.body: Apply every SQL migration to your Supabase project so multi-warehouse stock, registers, RLS, stock_alerts, and CSV paths match the app you deploy. Set VITE_* variables for the correct Supabase URL and anon key; never expose the service role in the client. Sign in with your bootstrap admin (see Platform guide → security). Confirm you can open Inventory and Admin before loading data.

operators_members.title: Create members (operators) and warehouse access
operators_members.body: Under Admin → Members, add each clerk or manager: username becomes their sign-in email pattern, password is stored in Auth only, and you pick allowed warehouses plus feature toggles (same switches as Control, stored as overrides on their profile). Operators without admin flag cannot open /control or /admin except via routes you explicitly grant. Do this early so you can test imports signed in as a non-admin user.

warehouses.title: Create warehouses and registers
warehouses.body: Define each storage location; codes are derived from the location text. Enable a cash register only where you truly take payments—POS checkout and some payment flows require a register-capable warehouse. Align warehouse codes with any CSV you will import. Assign every operator at least one allowed warehouse in Members.

categories_brands.title: Categories and brands (if needed)
categories_brands.body: Create categories and brands before or during product import. Product CSV can create missing brand/category names on the fly; pre-creating them keeps naming tidy.

people.title: Review people after the guided import
people.body: Use the guided paste wizard first (step 1). Then tidy roles, add anyone missing, and confirm old IDs are saved so a later sheet can fill phones or balances. Suppliers must exist before purchase-order CSV.

products.title: Import products and opening stock
products.body: Use Products → Import CSV. Set opening quantities per warehouse when you want live on-hand stock from day one (columns per warehouse code). Export CSV from the products page for a template. Resolve cost and list prices so later sales and PO lines stay coherent. Open a product after import to verify per-warehouse quantities.

inventory_transfers_guide.title: Plan stock transfers between warehouses
inventory_transfers_guide.body: If you split stock across sites, use Inventory → Stock transfers to move quantity with an auditable document (draft to posted). Run a few manual transfers after products exist to validate warehouse access for each operator. This is separate from purchase/sale documents.

data_sync_environments.title: Optional: sync local and hosted Supabase
data_sync_environments.body: When you run a local stack plus hosted production (or staging), enable “Data sync” in Control for trusted admins, then open /sync. Read the warnings on that screen: pushes overwrite target rows for mirrored business tables. Use history to see past runs. Skip this step if you only have a single cloud project.

payments_optional.title: Optional: standalone payments for opening balances
payments_optional.body: If you need opening customer or supplier balances on the ledger without tying to an order, use Payments → Import CSV where available. Complex split tenders from the old system are often easier to recreate in the UI than in bulk.

po_csv.title: Purchase orders (CSV)
po_csv.body: On Purchase orders → list, use Import CSV after suppliers and products exist. Choose Live (draft) for POs you will receive in the app—stock and payables update on confirm/receive. Choose Historical for backfill analytics only (no stock or supplier ledger). Use Export CSV on the same page for column headers.

orders_csv.title: Sales orders (CSV)
orders_csv.body: On Orders → list, use Import CSV after customers and products exist. Live creates drafts—stock and register change only when you complete/checkout like a normal order. Historical adds completed orders for charts without moving stock or posting register lines. Export CSV for a matching template.

register.title: Reconcile the register / cash drawer
register.body: Historical imports do not set physical cash. After cutover, compare the Register screen to your actual drawer and use deposits or withdrawals (if your process allows) so tender balances match reality. Link payments to the correct register warehouse when recording money in.

smoke_test.title: Smoke test in the live flows
smoke_test.body: Create one small draft sale and one draft PO in the normal screens, then complete them end-to-end. Verify stock movement, person balance, and register lines match expectations before relying on bulk data.

control_review.title: Review Control (feature flags)
control_review.body: Open Control and confirm which CSV imports, hub shortcuts, POS actions, purchase-order receive/cancel, edit-as-replacement, and admin shortcuts match each role. Remember: toggles hide UI; Members overrides still apply per user. Tighten anything you do not want during stabilization.

documentation_review.title: Skim the Platform guide
documentation_review.body: Open Admin → Documentation and walk the feature map so trainers know where orders, POs, payments, transfers, alerts, and security behaviors live. Keep the Migration guide link handy for the next store or environment you onboard.
